title: Newly opened top-level navigable isn't blessed for user activation
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/metadata/generated/element-a.https.sub.html is a test that checks for `sec-fetch-user` when user activation is set. That uses https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-user-activation which is based on https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#source-snapshot-params-activation which is the case when the window has https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#transient-activation set to true.

When implementing this in Servo and following the spec, I think the spec doesn't reflect what browsers do. What I was able to figure out:

1. A new window is created with `const win = window.open();`
2. The new window has target of `_blank`
3. https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable will create a new top-level navigable for this newly created window
4. An anchor is created inside of the document of that window
5. `test_driver.bless` is called
6. In it, since `context` is `null`, it uses `document`: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/16cc3039191861e50cb55b9d3a97f0b2b883c36f/resources/testdriver.js#L1273
7. `document` here is the document of the test, not the document in the newly created window that was opened
8. When it blesses the test document, it also does that for all descendent navigables: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#user-activation-processing-model:descendant-navigables
9. Since descendant navigables are only `<iframe>` within a document, not a window opened with `window.open()`, the `window` created in the test isn't blessed
10. When `anchor.click()` is invoked, the `document` of the test is blessed, but the newly created window is not. Thus the newly created window does not have user activation and Servo therefore fails this test. It would pass if I change the bless line to `test_driver.bless('enable user activation', () => anchor.click(), win);` to explicitly bless the newly created window.

All browsers currently pass this test, so my assumption is that when `window.open()` is called, it does create a top-level navigable, but it would receive the user activation blessing because it considers it a descendant navigable? It's not clear to me whether the test is wrong and browsers wrongly pass it, or the spec doesn't reflect what browsers do.
